knowledge_gaps.gap: Fundamental misunderstanding of logical OR operator, leading to an always-true condition and an infinite loop. The condition `(A || B)` is true if A is true OR B is true. If A is `nums[i] != 10` and B is `nums[i] != 20`, then if `nums[i]` is 10, A is false but B is true, so `false || true` is true. If `nums[i]` is 20, A is true but B is false, so `true || false` is true. If `nums[i]` is anything else, both A and B are true, so `true || true` is true. This means the loop will never terminate unless an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` occurs.

Incorrect loop control within the `while` loop. The loop's index `i` is not incremented inside the `while` block, causing it to repeatedly process the same array element. This, combined with the always-true condition, results in an infinite loop.
